newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Bolger should force NZ First's hand - Prebble.
newsitem.headline: Bolger should force NZ First's hand - Prebble.

text.p: Act party leader Richard Prebble said on Wednesday Prime Minister Jim Bolger should force New Zealand First to declare its hand on likely coalitions.

The new Wellington Central MP said Bolger could go to Governor-General Sir Michael Hardie Boys and ask for the chance to form a government. That would test support in parliament almost immediately, he said.
Prebble said Bolger was clearly prepared to look at the nationalist New Zealand First's position before he went to the Governor-General, but he should not let that process move into instability.

"After he's had a look at the demands that are being made, that is an option that is open to him. If it becomes clear that it's destabilising, then I think it's an option that he should follow," Prebble told Radio New Zealand.
Both the ruling conservative National party and the main opposition Labour party have said they aim to form a government with support from New Zealand First.
NZ First leader Winston Peters is keeping the country guessing which way his party will leap, saying it will not necessarily be harmful if the negotiating process drags on until Christmas.
United MP Peter Dunne earlier said that National should call New Zealand First's bluff, rather than submit to blackmail over terms for coalition. -- Wellington Newsroom 64 4 4734746
